stem: The marks scored by eight students in a class test are: 34, 57, 22, 68, 45, 71, 29, 53. The range of the marks is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student reads maximum as 69 instead of 71 and computes 69 - 22 = 47.
Student confuses minimum with second-smallest (29) and computes 68 - 24 or uses 71 - 27 = 44 due to a misread.
Student computes 71 - 29 = 42, using the second-smallest value (29) as the minimum instead of 22.

explanation: Range requires only the two extreme values. Maximum = 71, minimum = 22. Range = 71 - 22 = 49.

explanation_sections.punchline: Always identify both extremes carefully; the minimum here is 22, not 29.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify range = Max - Min. Sort or scan: min = 22, max = 71. Range = 71 - 22 = 49.
explanation_sections.lesson: When values are unsorted, list them in order or explicitly mark the smallest before subtracting.
explanation_sections.timing: 25 seconds. Write out the sorted list mentally; the trap is picking 29 as the minimum, giving 42.
